description: Semantic search eval fixtures. Authored 2026-09-09 in the presets session (recommendation 2026-09-08-002 §10 Session 3), replacing the two-query stub that landed with the rig in Phase Search V2 Cluster B (B6). Sixteen entries in two halves. PRESET half (8, diagnostic): the `phrase` each preset card sends to the engine when the search_semantic flag is on, copied verbatim from src/lib/content/presets.ts, with the user-facing `sentence` recorded alongside it. TITLE half (8, gating): a title a user would plausibly type. Expected sets were curated from the live catalogue on 2026-09-09 by objective criteria — genre, runtime, rating and vote floors, availability for the free entry — and deliberately NOT from what the engine already returns, so the fixture measures retrieval rather than confirming it. Every expected tmdb_id was verified present in `titles` with a non-null embedding.
_thresholds_note: Thresholds apply to the GATING (known-title) entries only, and are set from the measured baseline of 2026-09-09 with margin: p@10 1.00 and MRR 0.90 across all eight, so 0.9/0.75 catches a real regression without failing on noise. The stub's 0.6/0.7 were written before any query had ever been run. The preset entries are DIAGNOSTIC, not gating, and the reason is measurable rather than convenient: they are scored against six or seven hand-picked titles out of a six-figure catalogue, so an answer that is entirely good but picks DIFFERENT good titles scores zero. Measured that day, every preset phrase scored p@10 = 0.00 against these sets while returning results that read correctly by eye — the `slow` phrase returned Small Things Like These, The Quiet Girl and I'm Thinking of Ending Things, and the `late` phrase returned The Haunting of Hill House and Marrowbone. Gating on that number would fail the build for being right. The same run produced the finding that justifies keeping `phrase` and `sentence` distinct: the short SENTENCES retrieve near-literal word matches rather than the intent — 'something fast and fun' returned the Fast & Furious franchise, 'something easy and warm I can half-watch' returned Hot Frosty and Melting Me Softly, and 'something long and absorbing I can sink into' returned The Abyss and Deep Sea. That is the free-text (described) route's weakness, it is why the route ships behind the search_semantic flag with a visible 'Search titles instead' escape, and it is the strongest argument for the Worker-side query-understanding step in §8.2.

queries.query: an understated, meditative drama that unfolds gradually and rewards your attention — thoughtful, restrained, character-driven and emotionally rich
queries._note: Long (>120 min), highly rated, character-led drama with no action lead. Popularity-ordered candidates were pruned by hand: Django Unchained and Inglourious Basterds are long and well rated but are not what 'sink into' means.
queries.sentence: something long and absorbing I can sink into

queries.query: an exciting, high-energy crowd-pleaser — thrilling, entertaining and effortless to enjoy, an adrenaline-fuelled popcorn film
queries._note: Action/adventure crowd-pleasers. Inception and Interstellar are excluded on purpose despite topping the same genre query — 'don't have to think' rules them out, and the engine putting them first would be a real miss.
queries.sentence: something fast and fun where I don't have to think

queries.query: an eerie, unsettling and atmospheric horror or thriller — creepy, ominous, mysterious, tense and haunting
queries.sentence: something dark and strange for late at night

queries.query: a heartwarming, gentle and uplifting film — sweet, charming, tender and reassuring, an easy and soothing watch
queries._note: The comedy+romance genre query returns Pulp Fiction and The Wolf of Wall Street near the top on vote count alone. Neither is 'easy and warm'; both are excluded, which is the point of curating rather than taking the head of a popularity list.
queries.sentence: something easy and warm I can half-watch

queries._note: The QUERY here is the card's sentence, not its phrase, because the phrase was retired on 2026-09-09 and the card now carries `phrase: null` — the sentence is the only text from this card an embedding can still see, via free-text routing on the described route. Same shape as the `free` entry below, and kept for the same reason: as the measured evidence for a filter-only card. THE RETIRED PHRASE WAS "a recent, well-reviewed film or series from the last year that both critics and audiences rated highly", and it scored p@10 0.00 / rr 0.00 with a top five of Voir (a documentary series in which film lovers examine cinematic moments), The Favourite, The Great, Blockbuster and Nightcrawler — surface matches on the vocabulary of acclaim, none recent, none chosen for being well-reviewed. A statement ABOUT a title is not a description OF one, and no synopsis reads like it. On a device that neighbourhood, post-filtered by recency and rating, left TWO titles out of 363 in the catalogue meeting the card's own criteria. Expected set is 2024–2025, vote_average >= 7.2, vote_count >= 2500. A future session that gives this card a phrase should have to justify it against these numbers.

queries.query: something I don't have to pay for
queries._note: EXPECTED TO BE THE WEAKEST ENTRY, and kept for exactly that reason. Cost is a fact about availability, not a property any embedding can carry, so this sentence has no semantic answer — the expected set is simply well-rated titles verified as subscription-included on 2026-09-09. This is the measured evidence for the 'Free to watch' card carrying `phrase: null` and contributing only a filter (§2.3), and for the stream_type-aware RPC in migration 080. A future session that gives this card a phrase should have to justify it against this number.
queries.sentence: something I don't have to pay for

queries.query: a tight, satisfying, self-contained film under two hours
queries._note: Self-contained films of 85–118 minutes, rating >= 7.6. Runtime is enforced by the preset's filter in the product; this measures the phrasing alone.
queries.sentence: a film I can actually finish tonight

queries.query: a warm, funny family film or series that adults enjoy as much as children — nothing frightening or adult
queries.sentence: something we can all watch together

queries._note: The known-title half exists to calibrate the title-hit threshold in src/lib/search/titleHit.ts (§9.2 routing rule 2). Each of these is a title a user would plausibly type; the engine should return it first, and the app should never send it to the engine at all.
